defect: build_owner_recompiler filtered the owner's changed refs by the consumed (authority_id, authority_version) tuple. In a v1->v2 promotion the owner reports changed = (prior_v1, selected_v2), so the filter selected the PRIOR consumed ref and passed it to recomposition as the alleged successor.
repair: Resolve the exact consumed prior ref by identity membership in the owner's changed set, not by id+version tuple.
Resolve the unique OTHER changed ref sharing that authority identity as the governed successor.
Never by tuple position and never by version label.
Require the successor to be an authority the owner actually knows (registered snapshot), which forbids future or unknown authority pre-binding.

fixture_identity_defect.description: build_model_authority_transition exposed both a separately synthesized revised-model ref and the candidate-derived revision.proposed_authority_ref, and courts used them interchangeably.
fixture_identity_defect.severity: the separately synthesized decoy ref shares the CONSUMED prior's authority_content_hash (4d565f1b), differing only in version label and fingerprint, because revised_model_authority_snapshot copies the base content hash
fixture_identity_defect.consequence: choosing the decoy recomputes the product under the authority it already consumed, so no identity change would be observable
correction: the fixture now exposes unsealed_decoy_model_ref and sealed_successor_ref as distinct, explicitly named values
sealed_successor_of() resolves the successor through the owner and asserts it differs from the consumed prior
six existing court references that passed the decoy as the successor were corrected to the sealed successor
build_model_rule_from_sealed_successor() builds the consumer model rule bound to the exact governed successor
